definition: Social adaptation is how well a person manages and fits into social life. In this packet, it is described as involving interpersonal skills and being linked to the quality of social interactions and mental health.

reasons: The packet only states that interpersonal skills are an important component of college students’ social adaptation; it does not define social adaptation as “how well a person manages and fits into social life.”

The claim that social adaptation itself is “linked to the quality of social interactions and mental health” overstates the packet, which says interpersonal skills are associated with those outcomes, not social adaptation generally.

The definition says “Social adaptation is how well a person manages and fits into social life,” but the packet does not provide this general wording or a direct definition of social adaptation as “managing and fitting into social life.”

The definition asserts that, in the packet, social adaptation “is described as involving interpersonal skills and being linked to the quality of social interactions and mental health.” The packet supports that interpersonal skills are associated with the quality of social interactions and mental health, but it does not explicitly define social adaptation itself as “involving interpersonal skills” beyond describing interpersonal skills as an important component related to social adaptation in college students.

The packet’s content is framed specifically around “college students,” whereas the definition presents a general “a person” formulation; the packet does not justify generalizing beyond college students.
